The Federal Government has commenced the distribution of starter kits to “7,000 graduates of its Technical and Vocational Education and Training initiative in Lagos State to enable them to establish businesses and become self-employed.” The Minister of Education, Dr Tunji Alausa, disclosed this on Friday during the graduation and starter-kit handover ceremony at the Federal Technical College, Yaba, Lagos. He said, “87,701 trainees had successfully completed the first cohort of the programme nationwide, while 150,000 participants had been admitted into the second cohort following 1.49 million applications.” Alausa said the provision of starter kits was intended to bridge the gap between skills acquisition and economic opportunities by equipping graduates with the tools to establish businesses, earn incomes and create employment for others. He stated, “Acquiring a skill is a vital first step, but access to tools can determine how quickly that skill becomes a source of income. Make PUNCH part of your everyday experience. Add us to your Preferred Sources “The provision of starter kits is therefore an integral part of this initiative. These are productive assets intended to help beneficiaries begin work, serve customers and build viable enterprises.” The minister said the initiative was also designed to address the country’s demand for skilled workers, stressing that Nigeria needed technicians, electricians, artisans and entrepreneurs capable of supporting industry and economic development. “Technical and vocational education provides a practical route to these opportunities and deserves sustained investment and public respect,” he said. Alausa explained that the distribution would continue in phases as beneficiaries completed the required assessment and verification processes. He clarified that completing training, obtaining certification and meeting the requirements for starter-kit support were separate stages. The minister added that the success of the programme would be measured by graduates securing employment, establishing businesses, improving their earnings and creating opportunities for others. He also called on state governments, community leaders and private-sector organisations to support the graduates through mentorship, practical experience and recruitment opportunities. In her remarks, the Director overseeing the Office of the Permanent Secretary, Dr Folake Olatunji-David, represented by the Director of Technology and Science Education, Mrs P.O. Ogungbemi, said the initiative was designed to bridge the gap between educational qualifications and labour-market demands. One of the beneficiaries, Feyisayo Onafowokan, who trained in leatherwork and shoemaking, described the programme as life-changing, saying it had provided her with an opportunity to overcome unemployment and establish a means of livelihood. The TVET initiative is part of the Federal Government’s efforts under President Bola Tinubu’s Renewed Hope Agenda to address youth unemployment, strengthen technical skills and promote entrepreneurship through practical, industry-relevant training. The programme covers trades including welding and fabrication, electrical installation, automobile mechanics, solar photovoltaic installation, fashion design, ICT, agriculture, hospitality and leatherwork.
